---
title: OpenAI compatibility
---

Connect OpenAI clients to Ollama. Ollama supports a subset of the [OpenAI API](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference).

## Direct cloud access

Set your [API key](https://ollama.com/settings/keys) in `OLLAMA_API_KEY`. Install the client with `pip install openai`. No Ollama installation required.

```python
import os
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://ollama.com/v1",
    api_key=os.environ["OLLAMA_API_KEY"],
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="gemma4:31b",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello in one sentence."}],
)
print(response.choices[0].message.content)
```

The same client supports stateless Responses requests:

```python
response = client.responses.create(
    model="gemma4:31b",
    input="Say hello in one sentence.",
)
print(response.output_text)
```

Choose a [cloud model](https://ollama.com/search?c=cloud). The cloud API does not support stateful Responses, built-in web search through `/v1/responses`, or custom/freeform tool-call replay.

## Local server usage

These examples connect to your local Ollama server. The client requires an API key value, but Ollama ignores it. To use cloud models through this server, [sign in to Ollama](/api/authentication#signing-in).

### Simple `/v1/chat/completions` example

<CodeGroup dropdown>

```python basic.py
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url='http://localhost:11434/v1/',
    api_key='ollama',  # required but ignored
)

chat_completion = client.chat.completions.create(
    messages=[
        {
            'role': 'user',
            'content': 'Say this is a test',
        }
    ],
    model='gpt-oss:20b',
)
print(chat_completion.choices[0].message.content)
```

```javascript basic.js
import OpenAI from "openai";

const openai = new OpenAI({
  baseURL: "http://localhost:11434/v1/",
  apiKey: "ollama", // required but ignored
});

const chatCompletion = await openai.chat.completions.create({
  messages: [{ role: "user", content: "Say this is a test" }],
  model: "gpt-oss:20b",
});

console.log(chatCompletion.choices[0].message.content);
```

```shell basic.sh
curl -X POST http://localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d '{
  "model": "gpt-oss:20b",
  "messages": [{ "role": "user", "content": "Say this is a test" }]
}'
```

</CodeGroup>

### `/v1/chat/completions` with vision example

<CodeGroup dropdown>

```python vision.py
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url='http://localhost:11434/v1/',
    api_key='ollama',  # required but ignored
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model='qwen3-vl:8b',
    messages=[
        {
            'role': 'user',
            'content': [
                {'type': 'text', 'text': "What's in this image?"},
                {
                    'type': 'image_url',
                    'image_url': 'data:image/png;base64,',
                },
            ],
        }
    ],
    max_tokens=300,
)
print(response.choices[0].message.content)
```

```javascript vision.js
import OpenAI from "openai";

const openai = new OpenAI({
  baseURL: "http://localhost:11434/v1/",
  apiKey: "ollama", // required but ignored
});

const response = await openai.chat.completions.create({
  model: "qwen3-vl:8b",
  messages: [
    {
      role: "user",
      content: [
        { type: "text", text: "What's in this image?" },
        {
          type: "image_url",
          image_url:
            "data:image/png;base64,",
        },
      ],
    },
  ],
});
console.log(response.choices[0].message.content);
```

```shell vision.sh
curl -X POST http://localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d '{
  "model": "qwen3-vl:8b",
  "messages": [{ "role": "user", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "What is this an image of?"}, {"type": "image_url", "image_url": "data:image/png;base64,"}]}]
}'
```

</CodeGroup>

## Endpoints

### `/v1/chat/completions`

#### Supported features

- [x] Chat completions
- [x] Streaming
- [x] JSON mode
- [x] Reproducible outputs
- [x] Vision
- [x] Tools
- [x] Reasoning/thinking control (for thinking models)
- [ ] Logprobs

#### Supported request fields

- [x] `model`
- [x] `messages`
  - [x] Text `content`
  - [x] Image `content`
    - [x] Base64 encoded image
    - [ ] Image URL
  - [x] Array of `content` parts
- [x] `frequency_penalty`
- [x] `presence_penalty`
- [x] `response_format`
- [x] `seed`
- [x] `stop`
- [x] `stream`
- [x] `stream_options`
  - [x] `include_usage`
- [x] `temperature`
- [x] `top_p`
- [x] `max_tokens`
- [x] `tools`
- [x] `reasoning_effort` (model-defined names and compatibility aliases)
- [x] `reasoning`
  - [x] `effort` (model-defined names and compatibility aliases)
- [ ] `tool_choice`
- [ ] `logit_bias`
- [ ] `user`
- [ ] `n`

`reasoning_effort` and `reasoning.effort` control model thinking. Use `/api/show` to discover each model's supported values and default. When a model uses its metadata to resolve named levels, supported names are applied exactly and unsupported names resolve to the model default. Boolean-only models that support enabling thinking map recognized compatibility efforts to `true`, while `"none"` requests `false`. Models without metadata retain the existing compatibility aliases: `"minimal"` maps to `"low"`, and `"xhigh"` or `"ultra"` map to `"max"`. GPT-OSS keeps its existing OpenAI compatibility conversion: `"minimal"` uses `"low"`, `"xhigh"` or `"ultra"` use `"high"`, and `"none"` requests no thinking output.

### `/v1/completions`

#### Supported features

- [x] Completions
- [x] Streaming
- [x] JSON mode
- [x] Reproducible outputs
- [ ] Logprobs

#### Supported request fields

- [x] `model`
- [x] `prompt`
- [x] `frequency_penalty`
- [x] `presence_penalty`
- [x] `seed`
- [x] `stop`
- [x] `stream`
- [x] `stream_options`
  - [x] `include_usage`
- [x] `temperature`
- [x] `top_p`
- [x] `max_tokens`
- [x] `suffix`
- [ ] `best_of`
- [ ] `echo`
- [ ] `logit_bias`
- [ ] `user`
- [ ] `n`

#### Notes

- `prompt` currently only accepts a string

### `/v1/models`

#### Notes

- `created` corresponds to when the model was last modified
- `owned_by` corresponds to the ollama username, defaulting to `"library"`

### `/v1/models/{model}`

#### Notes

- `created` corresponds to when the model was last modified
- `owned_by` corresponds to the ollama username, defaulting to `"library"`

### `/v1/embeddings`

#### Supported request fields

- [x] `model`
- [x] `input`
  - [x] string
  - [x] array of strings
  - [ ] array of tokens
  - [ ] array of token arrays
- [x] `encoding format`
- [x] `dimensions`
- [ ] `user`

### `/v1/audio/speech`

> Note: Added in Ollama v0.40.8

Generates audio with [speech models](/capabilities/speech). Upstream
[Phonon support](https://github.com/ollama/ollama/pull/19166) introduced this
endpoint, CLI playback and streaming audio. This fork extends that infrastructure
to native MLX Qwen3-TTS, Kokoro, Voxtral TTS and Chatterbox models.

#### Standard request fields

- [x] `model` (an installed speech model)
- [x] `input` (1–4,096 characters)
- [x] `voice` (a model-specific string; required reference-conditioned models use `reference_audio` instead)
- [x] `response_format`: `wav` (default) or `pcm`
- [x] `speed` (default `1`; model-specific limits below)
- [x] `instructions` (Qwen3-TTS 1.7B CustomVoice only; at most 1,024 characters)
- [x] `stream_format`: `audio` only

| Model | Voice / conditioning | Speed | Instructions |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Phonon | Named preset or its default voice | `1` | Unsupported |
| Qwen3-TTS CustomVoice 0.6B / 1.7B | Preset; omission selects `Ryan` | `1` | 1.7B only |
| Qwen3-TTS Base 0.6B / 1.7B | Reference audio and matching transcript required; omit `voice` | `1` | Unsupported |
| Kokoro 82M | English preset; omission selects `af_heart` | `0.5`–`2` | Unsupported |
| Voxtral TTS | Preset matching the language; default `casual_male` for English | `1` | Unsupported |
| Chatterbox multilingual v3 | Reference audio required; omit `voice` | `1` | Unsupported |
| Chatterbox Turbo | `default` preset, or reference audio with `voice` omitted | `1` | Unsupported |

Use `ollama show <model>` or `/api/show` to discover `voices`, `languages` and
`voice_languages`. A preset name from another model is not interchangeable.
Voxtral's requested language must match its voice. Kokoro supports English;
Chatterbox v3 currently supports English/German and Turbo supports English.

#### Ollama extensions

- `language`: output language, where supported by the model.
- `seed`: unsigned sampling seed for the added native MLX models. It does not
  imply identical random draws or audio across different runtimes.
- `reference_audio`: `{ "format": "wav", "data": "<base64-encoded complete WAV>" }`.
  Reference WAVs must be mono PCM16, 16–48 kHz, at most 15 seconds. Turbo requires
  more than 5 seconds; v3 requires at least 0.1 seconds. Reference audio cannot
  be combined with `voice`.
- `reference_text`: matching reference transcript, required by Qwen3-TTS Base,
  at most 4,096 characters. Chatterbox rejects this field.

The entire JSON request, including base64 audio, is limited to 4 MiB. The CLI
reads local reference files; the server accepts audio bytes, never a local path.
These reference fields do not implement OpenAI's stored custom-voice resources.

#### Compatibility boundaries

Audio is 16-bit mono at 24 kHz; `pcm` is little-endian samples without a header.
Responses stream audio bytes, not SSE. WAV/PCM-only output, the WAV default and
audio-only streaming originated with upstream Phonon support. `mp3`, `opus`,
`aac`, `flac`, `stream_format: "sse"` and voice-ID objects are unsupported.
Unsupported options return `400` rather than being silently ignored.

This is a supported subset of the
[OpenAI speech API](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/audio/subresources/speech/methods/create),
with explicit Ollama extensions. OpenAI's default format, voice forms, available
formats and instruction limit differ. Speech streaming does not establish
OpenAI Realtime API compatibility.

### `/v1/audio/transcriptions`

Transcribes speech with models that accept audio input.

#### Supported request fields

- [x] `file` (WAV at up to 384 kHz; up to 512 MB and 2 hours)
- [x] `model`
- [x] `language` (ISO 639-1 code such as `fr`, or an English language name; omit it to let the model detect the language)
- [x] `prompt` (used by models without speech-specific instructions)
- [x] `response_format`
  - [x] `json` (default)
  - [x] `text`
  - [x] `verbose_json` (one segment per transcribed piece of audio; `language` is the output language for translations; for transcriptions it is set only when given in the request)
  - [ ] `srt`, `vtt`
- [x] `temperature` (default `0`)
- [x] `stream` (server-sent `transcript.text.delta` and `transcript.text.done` events)
- [x] `timestamp_granularities[]` (`segment`, or experimental `word` timestamps with native Qwen3-ASR and ForcedAligner; requires `verbose_json` and non-streaming output)

#### Notes

- Audio longer than the model takes at once (30 seconds for current models) is split at pauses and transcribed piece by piece. Streaming sends each piece as it finishes.
- Each model gets the transcription instructions its publisher documents.

For experimental word timestamps, configure `OLLAMA_ALIGNMENT_MODEL` on the server
or pass the Ollama extension `alignment_model` in the request. Word mode accepts
complete English/German WAV or MP3 recordings up to two hours and 512 MiB per request.

#### Native Qwen3-ASR and word timestamps

This fork imports the original `Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B`, `Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-1.7B` and
`Qwen/Qwen3-ForcedAligner-0.6B` checkpoints in an MLX-enabled build on Apple
Silicon. Original BF16 weights remain unchanged on disk; native execution
promotes them to F32. The ASR models transcribe audio; ForcedAligner supplies
timestamps for text and is not a replacement transcription model.

Create persistent Modelfiles pointing at each downloaded original snapshot,
using the same local-directory import pattern as
[speech models](/capabilities/speech#original-mlx-checkpoints):

```shell
ollama create --experimental qwen3-asr:0.6b -f ./Modelfile.qwen3-asr-0.6b
ollama create --experimental qwen3-asr:1.7b -f ./Modelfile.qwen3-asr-1.7b
ollama create --experimental qwen3-forced-aligner:0.6b -f ./Modelfile.qwen3-forced-aligner-0.6b
```

Each Modelfile contains `FROM <original-snapshot-directory>` for its respective
repository. No Python conversion or temporary prepared directory is required.
These are original floating-point imports, not newly qualified quantizations.

Native ASR is qualified for English/German complete WAVs, with automatic
language detection when `language` is omitted. It supports up to 60 seconds
per generation; longer ordinary uploads use the existing clip segmentation,
whose cross-boundary recognition quality is not qualified. It does not support
the translation endpoint. `prompt` supplies the ASR system context; `stream=true`
sends completed clip text after upload and inference, not live incoming audio.

Word timestamps use the standard
[OpenAI timestamp parameter and word shape](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/audio/subresources/transcriptions/methods/create).
An installed native ForcedAligner is additionally required. Set
`OLLAMA_ALIGNMENT_MODEL=qwen3-forced-aligner:0.6b` when starting the server, or
use `alignment_model` as an optional Ollama request extension:

```shell
curl http://localhost:11434/v1/audio/transcriptions \
  -F model=qwen3-asr:1.7b \
  -F file=@recording.wav \
  -F language=de \
  -F response_format=verbose_json \
  -F 'timestamp_granularities[]=word' \
  -F alignment_model=qwen3-forced-aligner:0.6b
```

Word mode accepts a complete WAV or MP3 upload, up to two hours of decoded audio
and 512 MiB per request, with `response_format=verbose_json` and `stream=false`
(the default). WAV recordings up to 60 seconds retain the existing single-clip
behavior. Longer recordings use 30-second ownership intervals with two seconds
of overlapping audio context on each side. MP3 decoding is native; FFmpeg and
Python are not server dependencies. Unsupported/corrupt audio fails the request.

Decoded audio is read incrementally from the temporary upload file. The rolling
buffer retains at most 60 seconds plus one source sample; only a bounded window
is resampled and passed to the ASR/aligner at a time. Text/word output grows with
recording length, within the two-hour cap. Upload files and decoders are closed
on success, cancellation or error; scheduler leases remain held until positive
native cleanup. A cancelled request returns no partial successful transcript.

Words crossing a chunk cut are aligned with surrounding context and assigned
by their interval midpoint. All times include the window's global sample offset.
Matching boundary words with intersecting intervals are emitted once; repeated
words at disjoint times are retained. Conflicting overlapping words fail with
HTTP 422 rather than fabricating/clamping timestamps. These controls do not
guarantee recognition or alignment accuracy at every boundary. Repeat `timestamp_granularities[]` with `segment` to
include both word and globally offset segments for retained chunk text. The server does not download or
discover an aligner automatically; `alignment_model` without word mode is
rejected.

The `words` entries contain `word`, `start` and `end`; times are seconds from
the recording's start. Words use the provider's normalized text, which can omit
punctuation and combining marks. Short-clip ASR `text` is retained exactly. Long-recording text is assembled from
owned word spans in the punctuated chunk transcripts. Invalid or
out-of-recording alignment fails the request; the server does not substitute
an untimed success. Provider agreement does not establish human-annotated
recognition or alignment accuracy.

`/api/experimental/audio/sessions` is a separate custom, default-disabled
protocol, enabled only by `OLLAMA_EXPERIMENT=asr-streaming`. It is not an OpenAI
Realtime endpoint. The closed live-caption commitment experiment does not
establish reliable continuous word commitment; ordinary transcription and
complete-file timestamps remain separate.

### `/v1/audio/translations`

> Note: Added in Ollama v0.40.12

Translates speech into text in another language.

#### Supported request fields

- [x] `file`
- [x] `model`
- [x] `to_language` (Ollama extension; ISO 639-1 code of the output language, default `en`)
- [x] `language` (Ollama extension; the spoken language, if known)
- [x] `prompt` (used by models without speech-specific instructions)
- [x] `response_format`, `temperature` and `stream`, as for transcriptions

### Responses API

`POST /v1/responses`

> Note: Added in Ollama v0.13.3

Ollama supports the [OpenAI Responses API](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/responses). Only the non-stateful flavor is supported (i.e., there is no `previous_response_id` or `conversation` support).

#### Supported features

- [x] Streaming
- [x] Tools (function calling)
- [x] Reasoning summaries (for thinking models)
- [ ] Stateful requests

#### Supported request fields

- [x] `model`
- [x] `input`
- [x] `instructions`
- [x] `tools`
- [x] `stream`
- [x] `temperature`
- [x] `top_p`
- [x] `max_output_tokens`
- [x] `reasoning`
  - [x] `effort` (model-defined names and compatibility aliases)
- [x] `think` (Ollama extension; boolean, model-defined string, or `null`)
- [ ] `previous_response_id` (stateful v1/responses not supported)
- [ ] `conversation` (stateful v1/responses not supported)
- [ ] `truncation`

## Models

For local inference, download a model before using it:

```shell
ollama pull llama3.2
```

Direct cloud requests use the identifiers from `https://ollama.com/api/tags` and do not require a pull. Through a signed-in local server, select a cloud model such as `gemma4:cloud`.

### Default model names on a local server

For tooling that relies on default OpenAI model names such as `gpt-3.5-turbo`, use `ollama cp` to copy an existing model name to a temporary name:

```shell
ollama cp llama3.2 gpt-3.5-turbo
```

Afterwards, this new model name can be specified the `model` field:

```shell
curl http://localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{
        "model": "gpt-3.5-turbo",
        "messages": [
            {
                "role": "user",
                "content": "Hello!"
            }
        ]
    }'
```

### Setting the local context size

The OpenAI API does not have a way of setting the context size for a model. If you need to change the context size, create a `Modelfile` which looks like:

```
FROM <some model>
PARAMETER num_ctx <context size>
```

Use the `ollama create mymodel` command to create a new model with the updated context size. Call the API with the updated model name:

```shell
curl http://localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{
        "model": "mymodel",
        "messages": [
            {
                "role": "user",
                "content": "Hello!"
            }
        ]
    }'
```
